newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bonds firm as more supply hits.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bonds firm as more supply hits.

text.p: U.S. corporate bond spreads held firm Friday afternoon amid another big injection of fresh paper and rapidly thinning activity, high-grades dealers said.
Some aggressively priced new issues from the week widened from original issue spreads, however.

Prices followed U.S. Treasuries higher following bond-friendly producer price data, traders said, but secondary trade paled next to governments. Credit markets were also preparing for a PSA recommended 1400 EDT/1800 GMT close on Friday and full close on Monday in observance of the U.S. Columbus Day holiday.

Topping the new issue slate, corporates were treated to $1.0 billion multi-tranche Baa3/BBB debt from New Corp's News America Holdings from lead manager Merrill Lynch & Co. The debt was priced in 12-, 20-, 40- and 100-year tranches at spreads over U.S. Treasuries of 90, 115, 135 and 146 basis points, respectively.

South Africa capitalized on favorable market tone and priced its first Yankee bond issue on Friday. The $300 million Baa3/BB-plus issue was priced as 8-3/8s at 99.156 for a spread of 195 basis points over the 10-year U.S. Treasury.

Commentary from trading desks was reminiscent of the entire week, with market participants reporting no erosion in market tone and investors laden with cash. Even so, some new issues eased when freed to trade.

Union Pacific Resources $200 million 30-year tranche was quoted at 66 basis point spread compared with 65 basis points on Thursday and the $200 million 10-years were quoted at 51 basis points compared with 49 basis points.
First Union National Bank's $300 million 10-year notes were quoted at 64 bid, 63 offer compared with an original issue spread of 59 basis points.

High-yielders were trading up 1/2 point on average with new issues leading the way, dealers said. As in high-grades, prices held up to brisk issuance this week and the promise of heavier volume through November, said one high-yield official.

"The market has done extremely well with what it's seen and the technicals continue to look very good," a high-yield desk manager said. "There's still a lot of cash coming into the market through mutual funds," he said, adding that the environment will attract more borrowers.
Energy sector issuance should be especially active, the manager said, with telecoms not far behind.
New issuance on Friday featured $200 million 10-year senior subordinated notes from Universal Outdoor Holdings Inc, priced as 9-3/4s to yield 9.85 percent or 325 basis points over the Treasury curve.

Reflecting market strength, Thursday's $500 million Paging Network senior subordinated notes of 2008 were quoted at 100-3/8 bid, 100-1/2 offer. The $275 million 10-year senior subordinated notes from U.S. Can Corp traded within a 101-7/8 bid, 102-1/2 market.
Freedom Chemicals' $125 million 10-year senior subordinated notes, priced late Thursday to yield 400 basis points over Treasuries, were quoted at 101-1/4 bid, 101-1/2 offer.
One issue saw its market fade, however. Outdoor System's $250 million 10-year notes were quoted at 99-3/8 bid, 99-3/4 offer at mid-session. The issue priced at par on Tuesday.
In the Treasury market, the long bond rose 1/2 point after the Labor Department said its producer price index rose 0.2 percent in September. The core was up 0.3 percent.
Also, the government said retail sales rose 0.7 percent in September following a revised 0.2 percent drop in August.
